identities.criterion: For every explicitly supplied PHP-FPM worker PID, the scanner and worker have identical effective UID/GID/groups, zero effective/permitted/ambient capabilities, matching project tree, mount namespace and Linux security context. Kernel access observations find no writable object or replaceable code root in the complete bounded configured app/vendor/lib inventory. Unsupported identity, seccomp, links or inventory gaps remain UNKNOWN.
identities.limitations: Run scanner as the actual unprivileged worker identity; root or differing identity is unsupported rather than a violation. All worker PIDs to be assessed must be explicitly supplied; no discovery-completeness claim. Unsupported worker mode, nonzero seccomp filters, sticky parent rules, external links or missing /proc permissions yield UNKNOWN. No code writes or privilege changes are performed. Original historical criterion and ID remain in the engineering backlog; this new ID records only its exact supported observation.

identities.criterion: Within the complete bounded configured upload path inventory, readable files contain no explicit long PHP opening tags or configured htaccess script-handler signatures and no PHP-like executable filename extension. identities.limitations: Default pub/media inventory is applicable without demanding absent optional import/export paths; explicitly add relevant roots. Original historical criterion and ID remain in the engineering backlog; this new ID records only its exact supported observation.

identities.criterion: In a nonempty bounded deployed authorization_role inventory and complete bounded authorization_rule inventory, every direct allow rule for Magento_Backend::all or Magento_Adminhtml::all assigned to a group role has a role ID in the explicitly configured approved_role_ids policy. Missing policy, malformed/orphan rows, direct user grants or incomplete tables remain UNKNOWN. This checks direct stored grants, not inherited effective privileges or business least privilege.
identities.limitations: Reads actual database tables through env.php connection; test PDO injects a real in-memory database, not assertion rows. No default approval list is invented; deployment owner must supply normal versioned policy configuration. Native global-group predicate deliberately does not claim full effective ACL/plugin authorization. Original historical criterion and ID remain in the engineering backlog; this new ID records only its exact supported observation.

identities.criterion: The supplied checkout path returns a successful same-origin no-redirect HTTPS GET with one unambiguous enforced Content-Security-Policy. The emitted policy explicitly defines script-src, connect-src, frame-src, form-action, object-src and base-uri; assessed sources contain no wildcard, unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or broad scheme-only source. object-src is exactly none, base-uri is exactly none or self, and reporting is present when configured. Report-only alone fails; redirect/inaccessible checkout, multiple policies, unsupported syntax or incomplete collection remain UNKNOWN.
identities.limitations: A redirect because no cart/session exists is UNKNOWN, not missing-CSP FAIL. Only named response is assessed; no checkout-wide or full browser execution guarantee. No state-changing requests, login, purchase or retained cookie/body content. Conservative explicit baseline can flag supported nonce plus unsafe-inline compatibility policy; title/criterion state exact Magebean policy, not universal CSP security judgment. Original historical criterion and ID remain in the engineering backlog; this new ID records only its exact supported observation.

identities.criterion: One successful same-origin no-redirect HTTPS GET at the configured path emits exactly one X-Content-Type-Options header whose trimmed value is nosniff. Missing or invalid header on an observed successful response fails; duplicate headers, redirects, transport failures and incomplete collection remain UNKNOWN. HSTS and frame protection are assessed separately.
identities.limitations: Nosniff plus existing HSTS/frame controls is not a claim of every security header on every route. No source-file union is used; runtime headers are collected directly with peer verification and bounded memory. Original historical criterion and ID remain in the engineering backlog; this new ID records only its exact supported observation.
